mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates a shift toward monetary easing, which lowers discount rates and increases present-value weights on future cash flows, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of expected cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during rate hikes are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% month-over-month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces growth expectations and compresses discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during labor weakness are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 1% month-over-month indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises growth expectations and compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during labor strength are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% month-over-month indicates weakening demand conditions, which compresses discount rates and reduces expected cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during demand contraction are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in consumer confidence (HOUST) above 105 points indicates improving demand conditions, which compresses discount rates and increases expected cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during high consumer confidence are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over 3 consecutive months indicates disinflation, which lowers inflation risk premiums and compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during disinflation are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above 1% month-over-month indicates stronger consumer demand, which compresses discount rates and increases expected cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during strong retail sales are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
